verses.1: A man, named Ananias, sold a property to his wife Saphira.
verses.2: And he also removed some of the hair from his head, as well as from his beard and hair on his body. He also placed something on the feet of the apostles.
verses.3: Peter said, “Ananias, why did Satan fill your heart with deceit? Why did you deceive yourself by believing in that holy spirit and being deceived by the honor of that place?”
verses.4: Didn’t you also hold great power in this world? Why then do you keep this matter in your heart? I swear by God, I’m not lying to anyone, but only to God himself.
verses.5: When Ananias heard these words, he became extremely angry. A great fear spread among all those who heard them.
verses.6: But the younger ones stood up and arrested him, and they buried him.
verses.7: And after three days, the woman came out of her hiding place. She was not wearing any clothes at all.
verses.8: Then Peter spoke to her. “Do you really give away such a large amount of land?” She replied, “Yes, indeed.”
verses.9: And Peter said to her, “Why do you ask for the spirit of the Lord to be tested by you? Look, the feet of those who are buried in the tomb are carrying that man toward the door and out through the doors.”
verses.10: It fell onto his feet, and it burned him completely. When the young men came along, they found her dead. So they buried her beside her husband’s body.
verses.11: And great fear spread throughout the entire church, and it affected everyone who heard these words.
verses.12: And because of the hands of the apostles, many signs and wonders took place among the people. And all those who lived in the city of Solomon’s Temple were united in their faith.
verses.13: But none of the others rushed to join them. Instead, the people supported them.
verses.14: But more importantly, they believed that the Lord had brought forth a large number of men and women.
verses.15: So that they could also carry the sick people into the squares and place them on stilts, so that when Peter arrived, his shadow could cover some of them.
verses.16: Also, the crowd from the surrounding cities of Jerusalem joined in as well. They brought those who were sick and suffering from harmful vapors. All of them were treated accordingly.
verses.17: But the high priest Anastasius and all those who were with him became enraged upon hearing about the plan of the Sadducees.
verses.18: And they placed their hands on the apostles, and they stood guard over them in public.
verses.19: But the angel of the Lord opened the doors of the prison at night, brought them out, and said:
verses.20: Go and stand there, and speak all the words related to this life in the holy place of the people.
verses.21: When they heard this, they went into the temple under the leadership of the high priest. The high priest and those who were with him called a meeting for all the elders of Israel. They sent them to the prison to be put to death.
verses.22: But those who were brought in as servants did not find them in the prison. Instead, they turned around and reported them.
verses.23: They said that the door was locked in all its secure places, and that the guards stood at the doors. But when they opened it from behind, they found no one inside.
verses.24: But when the priests and high priests heard these words, they wondered what could have caused such a thing to happen.
verses.25: And then, someone told them that the men who were imprisoned in the prison were actually those who lived in the temple and taught the people there.
verses.26: Then, the general went away with his officers, without using violence. He feared that the people might not obey him if he used force.
verses.27: They then brought them into the hall. And the high priest questioned them.
verses.28: We have requested that you not teach in the name of this man. It seems that you have fulfilled your duty to the Church by teaching there. Now, please bring over the blood of this man from us.
verses.29: Then Peter and the apostles replied, “It is better to obey God than men.”
verses.30: The God of our ancestors raised Jesus up. You yourselves saw Him being placed on a cross.
verses.31: Now, the Lord raised him to a position of leadership and salvation. He was given the task of bringing repentance to Israel and of removing their sins.
verses.32: And we too are witnesses of these miracles. It is the holy spirit that God has given to those who obey Him.
verses.33: But those who heard this were filled with envy and wanted to harm them.
verses.34: And one man who was present at the meeting, a Pharisee named Gamaliel, a respected teacher among the people, ordered that some people be brought outside to perform certain rituals.
verses.35: He also said to them, “Men of Israel, beware of what you are about to do to these people.”
verses.36: For those days, Theudas rose up, saying that he was someone who had gathered a number of men equal to four thousand. When he was killed, all those who were under his command also died, and became nothing.
verses.37: After this, Judas the Galilean stood up on the day of his arrest. He then turned back and saved the people from their fate. But everyone who tried to follow him also perished.
verses.38: And I say to you now: distance yourselves from these people, and get away from them. (For if this plan or action comes from human beings, then it will fail.)
verses.39: But if it comes from God, then you cannot defeat them. Even if you find some who are god-like among them. They were defeated by Him.
verses.40: And when they invited the apostles to come, they ordered them not to speak about Jesus’ name. They also dismissed them.
verses.41: Those who attended the meeting were happy, because they knew that they had been honored by being given such a title.
verses.42: They continued to teach and preach about Christ Jesus every day, both in the temple and also at people’s homes.
